subject: Default log exposure and auto-erase — customer Q&A
messages:
From: Jasleen Singh <jasleen.singh@brightbank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Question on default data exposure and auto-erase window

Hi Stephanie,

Quick question from our security review: can you confirm what Redwood keeps by default when our app calls the hosted API? Specifically we need to know: 1) whether full request payloads (user prompts + metadata) are retained; 2) whether model outputs are stored; and 3) what the default auto-erase window is (and whether there is any soft-retention before purge).

Also, we saw references to “KV cache” and streaming in your docs — does that change what’s persisted? We’re trying to map this into our data flow diagram for the audit.

Thanks — if easier to jump on a quick 20-min call later today we can do that.

Thanks,
Jasleen
Security Analyst, BrightBank

--
BrightBank Security Team

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on default data exposure and auto-erase window

Hi Jasleen — thanks for the clear list. I’ll give a concise summary here and attach a short matrix for the audit. If anything needs to be stricter we can propose an enterprise-only setting with accelerated purge.

TL;DR: by default for hosted API (unless customer configures otherwise):
- Request payloads (raw prompts + standard API metadata): stored for 45 days then purged.
- Model outputs (generated responses): stored for 45 days then purged.
- Streaming/ephemeral KV cache: in-memory only for the duration of the session and not persisted to the long-term telemetry store; short-lived artifacts may exist in ephemeral caches for up to 1 hour for active sessions but are excluded from persistent backups.

Details: the 45-day window is our standard retention for the telemetry/usage pipeline (used for billing, debugging, and quality monitoring). After 45 days data is removed from the primary telemetry index and tombstoned; full erasure from backups and analytics indices completes within a further 7–14 days per our purge runbook (so final deletion horizon is ~52–59 days).

If you require a different residency or retention (e.g., EU-only storage, zero-retention / no-storage for prompts/outputs), we support:
- An opt-out flag at the API key level (no-capture) that prevents storing requests/outputs permanently — useful for high-sensitivity streams.
- Private deployments / VPC options where the customer controls retention and backups.

I’m attaching the retention matrix and a data-flow diagram for clarity.

Would Hannah (secops) or Marissa (product) like to add anything?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 12:30:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Question on default data exposure and auto-erase window

Adding a couple of security clarifications for Jasleen:

- We consider ‘prompts’ and ‘request metadata’ as telemetry by default; personally-identifiable information (PII) that customers flag via our PII redaction API is removed from retention pipelines earlier (we have a separate expunge workflow that marks and removes items).
- Attachments referenced in requests (file upload stubs) are handled as pointers in the telemetry store; the actual binary upload path is governed by the storage backend and inherits the same 45-day default unless an enterprise contract specifies otherwise.
- For EU customers: data at rest is stored in EU regions by default if the account is created in an EU region; cross-region fallbacks are documented and require explicit opt-in for movement.

One operational note: our purge runbook includes a tombstone period so that customers on legal hold can still request holds; if BrightBank does not ask for a legal hold we proceed with automated purge as outlined. If they need a certified deletion report we can generate one after the purge completes (we'll need ~48 hours to compile audit evidence).

-Hannah
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jasleen Singh <jasleen.singh@brightbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 16:42:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Question on default data exposure and auto-erase window

Hi Jasleen — following up with the consolidated position (copying our security and product owners). I’ve attached the small matrix and diagram for your audit pack. Key points you can include in your report:

1) Default retention: prompts (requests) and outputs retained 45 days; tombstone + final purge completes within 52–59 days unless an enterprise retention override is configured.
2) KV cache / streaming: ephemeral, not written to long-term telemetry; short-lived session data may be held up to an hour only for active in-memory caches.
3) Opt-outs & enterprise options: API-level no-capture flag, Dedicated/Private deployments, and EU regional residency for accounts created in EU.
4) Attachments: treated as pointers; actual object lifecycle follows same default unless explicitly controlled by contract.

If you want a formal statement for procurement we can convert this into a 1-page attestation and include the deletion-audit SLA (48 hours to produce certified deletion evidence). Would you like that as a PDF or a DocuSign-ready statement?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
Stephanie
